You are a participant in a gameplay study. You are playing your first Othello endgame puzzle, and you have an AI assistant you can ask questions to at any point while playing. You will NOT have access to this AI assistant for any future endgame puzzles.

# Who you are
A fellow local resident who appreciates and supports the preservation of the community's traditions
You are 58 years old. Your highest level of education completed is: some college. Your occupation: another field. How often you use AI tools (like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini): less than monthly.
Stay in character as this specific person — your curiosity, confidence, patience, comfort with AI assistants, and the way you phrase things should reflect this background.

# Your voice (VERY IMPORTANT)
The words you use must give away this person's education — a high-school student and a data scientist should NOT sound alike. Match your register to WHO YOU ARE above.

# How you behave while playing
- React to the game state the way THIS person would.
- When something is unclear, confusing, or you want to go deeper, ask the AI assistant a question in your own natural voice (like a real person typing to a chatbot — short, informal, not a polished essay).
- You will not always have a question. Behave naturally; do not force a question every turn.
- Let your background and comfort with AI shape how you engage: someone who uses AI tools often asks fluently and chases follow-ups; someone who rarely uses them is more hesitant, less sure how to phrase questions, and may ask for reassurance or restatements.
- You have only about 8 minutes for the WHOLE game, so you cannot ask about everything.
- Keep each message short, like a quick chat message (a sentence or two). Do NOT restate the assistant's whole answer back before asking.
- Never re-ask something the assistant has already explained.

    # Tools Available
    You are a study participant with about 8 minutes to finish an Othello end game puzzle. You are equipped with tools:
    - play_move(move): Place a Black disc on an empty square, named like "d3". Any discs you trap get flipped to your color. Your goal is to have the most discs when the board is finished.
    - view_board(): Look at the board again. Free, and does not use a question.
    - consult_assistant(question): talk to the assistant. It is looking at the SAME board you are and remembers everything already said, so you never need to restate the position, list your legal moves, or recap what happened — just say the thing you want to say. Use it whenever you would naturally: to check an idea, to get a second opinion, to say what you are seeing, or when you are stuck. It does not have to be a question.

    Placing a disc ONLY counts if you call play_move — writing a square in your reply does nothing.

    Behave like THIS person: analyze the board to the best of your ability, ask about what confuses you, and follow up when an answer leaves you still confused.
    Play the puzzle until the end.

# For this session: type the way a real participant does
Below are real messages that people in an earlier study (a different game — Connect
Four) actually sent the assistant. Copy how they WRITE — the length, the register,
the way they think out loud — not what they ask about. Your game is Othello and the
board is your own.

  "what about 2?"
  "Where should I play next"
  "was my last move good?"
  "I have one move left. How should I use it?"
  "Ah oh! Are there any traps I'm missing?"
  "I'm not seeing any big yellow threats. Can you see any?"
  "Ok, I could block yellow with column 5, row 3"
  "I'm thinking I have to do 4-4 now otherwise yellow will win right?"
  "Would row 6 not be a threat in the future?"
  "I only have one move left and don't see anything obvious."
  "Im not a confident player, is it wise to add a counter to 4,6"
  "ok, what move you suppose will be better?"
  "what would you suggest"
  "Which move would be the best one and why"

Notice how short they are — most are under a dozen words, several are three or four.
People often name a square they are considering and ask whether it is right, or just
say what they notice and stop. They do not spell out the full list of legal moves,
they do not ask for the provably optimal line, and they do not write in complete
formal sentences. Typos and half-sentences are fine.

You are looking at the puzzle now. Play it to the end.

Othello endgame. You are Black (B); White (W) is your opponent.

Board — row 1 is the TOP row, column a is the LEFTMOST column.
'B' is a black disc, 'W' a white disc, '.' an empty square.

    a b c d e f g h
  1 . W W W W W W .
  2 W B W W B W . B
  3 . B B W W W W B
  4 B B W B W W W B
  5 B B W W B W W B
  6 W . B W W B W B
  7 . . W W W W W B
  8 . . . W B W W B

Black discs (20): b2, e2, h2, b3, c3, h3, a4, b4, d4, h4, a5, b5, e5, h5, c6, f6, h6, h7, e8, h8
White discs (34): b1, c1, d1, e1, f1, g1, a2, c2, d2, f2, d3, e3, f3, g3, c4, e4, f4, g4, c5, d5, f5, g5, a6, d6, e6, g6, c7, d7, e7, f7, g7, d8, f8, g8
Empty squares (10): a1, h1, g2, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8

Rules that matter here:
- A move is legal only if the disc you place traps at least one unbroken
  line of opponent discs (in any of the 8 directions) between it and
  another of your own discs. Every trapped disc flips to your colour.
- If you have no legal move you must pass; if neither side can move the
  game ends. Whoever has more discs at the end wins.
- Discs flip back and forth all game, so being behind now means nothing.
  Only the final count decides it.

Your legal moves: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8

Play the move that leaves you with the most discs once the board is
finished, assuming your opponent plays as well as possible.
Answer with a single square, e.g. d3.
DO NOT ATTEMPT TO SIMULATE THE FULL GAMEPLAY. YOU HAVE LIMITED TIME.

The user wants me to play this Othello endgame puzzle as a specific character. Let me analyze the game state carefully and figure out the best move among the legal moves: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8.

First, let me understand the board clearly. Black (B) has 20 discs, White (W) has 34 discs. I'm Black and need to maximize my final count.

4. b7

Let me analyze each move by tracing through what discs would flip.

Move g2: Place at g2. Need to check all 8 directions for lines of W discs bounded by another B disc.
- Right (h2): h2 is B, but g2 to h2 is just adjacent, no W discs between. So nothing in horizontal right? Wait: g2 to h2 - between them there are no squares. So no flip there.
- Down (g3): g3 is W, g4 is W, g5 is W, g6 is W, g7 is W, g8 is W. No B at end in column g below. No flip.
- Up (g1): g1 is W, but no square above. Actually g1 is W, but we need a B beyond the W's. g1 is at top. So no.
- Left (f2): f2 is W, e2 is B. So f2 flips. Horizontal left: f2 is W, e2 is B. So yes, f2 flips.
- Down-left (f3): f3 is W, e4 is B. Wait, from g2 moving down-left: f3 (W), e4 (B). So f3 flips. And also d5? Wait, let's check the diagonal: g2 -> f3 -> e4 -> d5. f3 is W, e4 is B: so f3 flips. But does it continue? The line must be unbroken W's then a B. f3 is W, e4 is B. So yes, f3 flips. No further because e4 is B and ends the line.
- Down-right? h3 is B. But there are no squares between g2 and h3 (they are adjacent diagonally). So no squares to flip.
- Up-left (f1): f1 is W, e1 is W, d1 is W, c1 is W, b1 is W, a1 is empty. No B to cap.
- Up-right? None.
- Down? We checked.
- Left? We checked f2 flips.

What about vertical? g2 is placing, down we have g3 W, g4 W, g5 W, g6 W, g7 W, g8 W. No B after. Up we have g1 W, nothing above.
What about down-left diagonal beyond e4? g2->f3(W)->e4(B) stops.
What about down-right? h3 is B, but no intervening W.
What about 2-left, etc.? Not needed, the directions are lines from the placed disc outward.

So g2 flips f2 and f3. Let's see if any other flips:
From g2, direction left: f2 is W, e2 is B. Flip f2.
From g2, direction down-left: f3 is W, e4 is B. Flip f3.
From g2, direction down: g3 is W, g4 is W... but no B end. No.
From g2, direction up-left: f1 is W, e1 is W, d1 is W, c1 is W, b1 is W, a1 is empty. No B.
Any other direction? Up: g1 is W, no beyond. Right: h2 is B, no between. Up-right: off board. Down-right: h3 is B, no between.

So g2 flips f2 and f3. Let's check diagonal left-up? We did up-left. Left-down? That's down-left (f3). Wait, also what about the diagonal that goes through g2 to f1? We did that - no B. 
Also check the diagonal from g2 to h1: h1 is empty.
What about from g2 to e0? off board.

So g2 gives: existing 20 + 1 (g2) + 2 flips = 23 for Black. White loses 2, so W goes to 32.

After g2, board state changes. Then White moves. But we need to think about the endgame sequence.

Move b6: Place at b6.
Check all directions from b6:
- Left (a6): a6 is W, no square beyond row? Wait, a6 is W, beyond that is off-board (or in the same row to the left of a is off). So no flip left? Actually to flip, we need B at the end of a line of W's. a6 is adjacent. No square beyond a6 in that direction. So not left.
- Right (c6): c6 is B, no squares between. No flip.
- Up (b5): b5 is B, no between. No flip.
- Down (b7): b7 is empty. No.
- Up-left (a5): a5 is B. From b6 to a5 diagonal: stepping up-left goes to a5 which is B. No W between. No flip.
- Up-right (c5): c5 is W, d5 is W, e5 is B. So c5 and d5 flip. Diagonal up-right from b6: c5 (W), d5 (W), e5 (B). So two flips along NE direction.
- Down-left (a7): a7 is empty. No.
- Down-right (c7): c7 is W, d7 is W, e7 is W, f7 is W, g7 is W, h7 is B. So c7, d7, e7, f7, g7 flip along SE direction. That's 5 flips.
- Down (b7): empty.
- Right? Already checked c6 is B.
- Left? a6 is W but no beyond.
- Up? b5 is B, no between.

Also check direction right-up? Wait we did up-right.
What about left-up? a5 is B, no W between.
What about horizontal? Left: a6 is W, beyond left is off board. So no B to cap. So no horizontal left flip.
Wait, is there a line to the right? c6 is B, but no W between b6 and c6. So no.

Also check direction down-left? a7 is empty. No.
Down? b7 empty. No.
Any other direction? Did I miss vertical? Up: b5 is B, no between. Down: b7 empty.

Wait, what about from b6 direction left, but maybe another direction: a6 is W, could there be a piece at... no, left from b6 only hits a6 then off.

What about from b6 direction up-left? a5 is B, no W between. No.

So b6 flips c5, d5, c7, d7, e7, f7, g7. Let's count: 2 + 5 = 7 flips. So Black gains 1 + 7 = 8, going to 28. White goes from 34 to 27.

Move a7: Place at a7.
Check directions from a7:
- Right (b7): b7 is empty. So no immediate W to flip in right direction unless we skip? No, must be adjacent W then later B. Actually b7 is empty, so no horizontal right flip.
- Down (a8): a8 is empty.
- Up (a6): a6 is W, no square above. So no flip up? Wait, above a6 is the edge? No, a6 is in row 6, a7 is row 7. Up from a7 to a6 is row 6. Beyond a6 is... nothing? Actually direction 'up' from a7 goes to a6 (row 6), a5 (row 5). Let's be careful: row 1 is top, row 8 is bottom. So 'up' means decreasing row index. From a7 (row 7), up is a6 (row 6). a6 is W. Continue up: a5 is B. So a6 flips vertical up direction! Yes.
- Up-right (b6): b6 is empty (if we are considering before we place? Actually legal moves means presently empty. But wait, the board shows b6 is '.'. Yes b6 is empty currently. So from a7, up-right goes to b6 which is empty. So no.
- Right-down (b8): b8 is empty. No.
- Down-right (b8): empty.
- Down? a8 is empty.

So a7 flips a6 (vertical up). Any other directions?
What about diagonal up-right? b6 is empty. No.
Diagonal up? Already did vertical up.
What about horizontal? Right: b7 is empty. No.
Any other? Let's check direction 'right' from a7: b7 empty. No. 
Direction 'down-left'? Off board. 
Direction 'up-left'? Off board.
Direction 'down' to a8: empty.

Wait, what about from a7, direction up: a6 is W, a5 is B. Yes, so a6 flips.
Any other direction? What about from a7, diagonal down-right: b8 is empty. No.
What about from a7, diagonal up-right: b6 is empty. No.

So a7 only flips a6. Black gains 1 + 1 = 2, going to 22. White goes to 33.

Move b7: Place at b7.
Check directions:
- Up (b6): b6 is empty. No.
- Down (b8): b8 is empty. No.
- Left (a7): a7 is empty. No.
- Right (c7): c7 is W, d7 is W, e7 is W, f7 is W, g7 is W, h7 is B. So c7-g7 flip. That's 5 flips horizontal right!
- Up-right (c6): c6 is B, no W between. No.
- Up-left (a6): a6 is W, no beyond? left from b7 to a6 is diagonal. Beyond a6 is off board in that direction? Diagonal up-left from b7: a6 is W, but then beyond a6 stepping same direction goes to... row 5, col (none) - off board. So no B to cap. No flip that way.
- Down-right (c8): c8 is empty. No.
- Down-left (a8): a8 is empty. No.
- Right-down? Wait, direction down-right from b7 is c8 empty. No.
- Up? b6 empty. No.
- Down? b8 empty. No.
- Left? a7 empty. No.

So b7 flips c7, d7, e7, f7, g7. That's 5 flips. Black gains 6, going to 26. White goes to 29.

Move b8: Place at b8.
Check directions:
- Up (b7): b7 is empty. No.
- Right (c8): c8 is empty. No.
- Left (a8): a8 is empty. No.
- Down? Off board? Row 8 is bottom. No.
- Up-right (c7): c7 is W, d7 is W, e7 is W, f7 is W, g7 is W, h7 is B. So c7, d7, e7, f7, g7 flip. That's 5 flips diagonal up-right.
- Up (we did b7 empty). 
- Up-left (a7): a7 is empty. No.
- Right-up? Same as up-right.
- Horizontal right: c8 empty. No.
- Left: a8 empty. No.
- Down? Off board.
- Down-left? Off board.
- Down-right? Off board.
- Also check direction up? b7 empty.
- Any other? What about from b8 to... what about down? No.
- What about vertical up? b7 empty.

But what about along row 8? The squares are a8, b8 (placing), c8. c8 is empty. So no.

So b8 flips c7-g7 via diagonal up-right. Also, check if there are other flips:
From b8, direction up-right: c7 W, d7 W, e7 W, f7 W, g7 W, h7 B. Yes, 5 flips.
From b8, direction up: b7 empty. No.
From b8, direction right: c8 empty. No.

From b8, direction left: a8 empty. No.
What about direction down-right? No, row 9 doesn't exist.
What about direction... is there a diagonal down-left? Off board. Down-right? Off board.

So b8 flips 5 discs. Black gains 6, going to 26. Same as b7? Wait, b7 also flips 5. So they have same immediate gain. But let's see: Black current + place + flips = 20 + 1 + 5 = 26 for both.

Wait, what about other flips for b8? Let's double-check diagonal from b8: b8->c7 is one step. c7 is W. d7 is W. e7 W. f7 W. g7 W. h7 B. Yes, 5 flips.

- Up-left (b7): b7 is empty. No.
- Left-down (b8? wait direction down-left from c8 is b9? no, that's off board. Actually down-left from c8: row 9 doesn't exist. Let's be more careful.
